newsitem.title: UK: Britain's main parties clash over job data leak.
newsitem.headline: Britain's main parties clash over job data leak.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives accused the opposition Labour Party of having obtained leaked information on Wednesday's market-sensitive unemployment figures and passed it to a national newspaper.
But the charge by Conservative chairman Brian Mawhinney was denied by a Labour employment spokesman.

Mawhinney published a letter he has written to Labour leader Tony Blair after the Labour-supporting Mirror reported the figures would show a fall of 57,800 in the number of benefit claimants in January.
The figures published at 0930 gmt in fact showed a drop of 67,800.
"It is now beyond doubt that your employment spokesman Ian McCartney obtained leaked information and gave it to the Daily Mirror," Mawhinney said.
"This is not only gross hypocrisy, but suggests your tacit approval of leaks by shadow ministers of market-sensitive material," he added, calling on Blair to sack McCartney if this was not the case.
But McCartney firmly denied being behind a leak to the Mirror. "I have no access in advance to the fiddled figures and I did not release them," he said.
Employment and Education Secretary Gillian Shephard said earlier she was setting up a government inquiry into the leak.

"Any leaking of sensitive financial information is very serious and of course risks serious consequences on the financial markets," she told a Conservative news conference. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
